title: The Fern Dance Hall band
summary: At 14 he joined the Fern Dance Hall band; he names the players and Bill Gillen, who imitated Bix's solo.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, my most important job after that, John, was in the Fern Dance Hall. And where was that? That was on Iberville, or as Dick says, Ziverville, on Iberville Street. And it was one of the leading dance halls in the city, always was, you know, and they had good jazz bands there. And I got the opportunity to play there. Of course, this was the big thing for me. I was about 14, just ready to turn 15, you know. And, I mean, this was a great big thing for me.
Can you just mention a few of the names?

Oh, yes. I remember, for sure, they had... Broken Dishes. Von Gammon. Oh, well, he's talking about my girlfriend now. Broken... I'm just kidding. She could have been. Broken Dishes, who really used to be a real tough girl. She used to beat up all the other girls, you know. She was tattooed. She was tattooed from head to foot. You know, the girls were working on tickets, you know. They'd try to beat one another out of dances, and she'd go back in, and she'd have it out with them. But it was all really part of the scene, I guess. It only added interest to it. But anyhow, you asked me about the band. The drummer was Von Gammon at the time I went there. He was the leader. Very nice person. And Harry Shields. Larry Shields' brother was playing clarinet. And a fellow by the name of Buzzy Willards playing banjo. A fellow by the name of Bill Gillen playing trumpet. Oh, incidentally, I might mention here, sounded a lot like Biggs.

Oh, Bill Gillen, he played a lot. What year was that? This was in 1920, about 1926, about 25, 26. And Bill Gillen was singing the blues solo, you know, that Biggs had made. And he got to, you know, people used to, all the musicians used to kid him about it. They used to call him Biggs. You know, they said, call him Biggs, play that solo for us, you know. And he did a great job on it. But somehow or another, he never followed music as a career.

I really don't know. I haven't seen him. God, I guess I haven't seen him in years. I know he, I never heard of him playing anywhere or playing any jobs. After I left the foreign, I never played with him again. That was the last time. But he played very well. And the bass, I don't think we had a bass.
So, that was it. Well, he, did he listen to Biggs records? Oh, yeah. I mean, he knew them.
Oh, he was a great admirer. Yes, he was a great admirer of Biggs. So, you see, Biggs was already making a big imprint on the people, the musicians down here.
